note: Do Mi Sol goes from a bare drill (3 minutes, the cap) to a tune that skips to singing chord notes over a band, so the longer singing time is musical. The drill goes through D, A and C from one Key row, keys that keep a beginner's Do Mi Sol low on the staff. Both staffs label their notes Do Re Mi, as the text names them, the band's chords can't be muted under the singer, and each step says what starts, what to sing on and what to do when an entry comes late.

exercise.title: Do Mi Sol: skip, sing a tune, sing over chords
exercise.focus: Do Mi Sol in D, A and C · an easy skipping tune · Do and Sol over D and A
exercise.why: Do, Mi and Sol are the three notes of the home chord, so the same skips come back in tune after tune: learn how they sound once and you can sing them in any key.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Start on a {{1}} that sits easily in your voice and sing {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} up and back down on the note names: they help you remember each sound. Then skip straight from {{1}} to {{5}}, and hold each note until your line settles on it.
Then tap A in the Key row above the staff and sing the same {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} over the new drone, then the same in C. The notes change, the pattern doesn't.
Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then press Play again and sing along on "la". Once it feels easy, sing it first and press Play to check.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the band: D and A take turns, one bar each. On "oo", sing {{1}} while the D box is lit and {{5}} while the A box is lit. If you come in late, hold your note and catch the next change. Then try {{3}} over D instead.
